keyframes.prompt: Vertical 2:3 nature macro photo at the muddy edge of a rice field pond, with a cut-away side view of the ground. The lower 40 percent of the frame is a side cross-section of soft wet dark grey-brown mud, with fine texture, a few tiny air holes and thin pale roots; the mud surface is a flat glistening line at 40 percent of the frame height. Above the mud, against a soft blurred green background of rice plants, two tall green sedge blades grow out of the mud near the left side; the taller blade rises and arches over to the right, so its upper part runs almost horizontally across the middle of the frame at about 70 percent of the frame height. Soft natural daylight from the upper left, sharp focus on the blade and the mud. On the arching blade, just right of the center of the frame, a large female horse fly stands, seen from the side: a stout grey-brown fly with very large compound eyes with iridescent green and purple bands, a grey thorax with faint dark stripes, a grey-brown abdomen with a row of pale triangles along the middle, clear wings held back over the body, about one sixth of the frame height long. Under the tip of its abdomen it is laying a small elongated mass of tiny white eggs stacked in neat layers on the blade, about one tenth of the frame height long. Keep everything important away from the left and right edges. Only one fly. No text, no watermark.
